messages:
diana: heads up — rolling v3.7.1 to eu-canary (5%) now, watch for latency and 5xx
deploy-bot: canary started: region=eu, pct=5, service=service-inference, release=v3.7.1
alice: seeing a small spike in 500s from pods in eu-canary, starting ~2m ago
ben: logs show config validation failures, snippet: "invalid config: unexpected field 'gpu_mode'"
carlos: confirm rollback policy: auto-rollback if error_rate > 2% for 5m?
infra-bot: monitoring rule fired at +4m: service-inference-eu error_rate=3.4% (5m)
deploy-bot: automated rollback attempted at +6m but stalled: gating job failed (schema-check)
diana: that gating job is the same one that pushed the new config — looks like schema drift between config-generator and runtime
pagerduty: PagerDuty alert triggered: SRE-EU-003 (high 5xx rate) — paging oncall
tina_oncall: I'm oncall — joining. quick triage: 500 payload shows runtime rejecting config on init -> crash + 502s upstream
alice: reproduced with curl to canary endpoint: HTTP/1.1 500
Response body: {"error":"invalid config: unexpected field 'gpu_mode'"}
ben: that field is injected by config-gen in release job. runtime's config schema didn't include it (we removed gpu_mode in last minor refactor)
diana: mitigation options: 1) revert release 2) patch canary config to remove gpu_mode 3) route traffic away from canary (drain)
tina_oncall: prefer full revert to be safe. can someone trigger manual rollback if deploy-bot is stuck?
deploy-bot: rollout paused due to gate failure; manual rollback permitted by policy with leader approval
carlos: manual rollback steps (short):
```bash
# rollback to stable tag
redwoodctl deploy rollback --service service-inference --region eu --to-tag stable-2026-03-16
# or kubectl rollout undo for kube deployment
kubectl -n infra rollout undo deploy/service-inference-eu
```
ben: I'll prepare the revert command and hold on final go from tina_oncall
infra-bot: note: if we do rollback, we should also revert the canary config in config-store to avoid reintroducing the field on next deploy
diana: assigning responsibilities: ben = execute rollback, alice = smoke verification, carlos = traffic routing/drain, tina_oncall = owner and customer communications
tina_oncall: go for rollback. ben please execute and post status updates
ben: executing rollback now (running redwoodctl...)
deploy-bot: manual rollback initiated by ben at +12m: target=stable-2026-03-16
ben: seeing new pods come up without the gpu_mode field, health checks passing on pod-level
carlos: starting traffic reroute to stable pool, draining canary
infra-bot: drain in progress — canary active connections=12 -> 0
alice: smoke tests: basic inference endpoints OK, 200s returning, latency back to baseline in eu-canary stable nodes
deploy-bot: rollback complete: canary pct=0, stable pct=100 (eu), release=stable-2026-03-16
diana: monitoring for 10m to ensure error rate stays low. good job team
pagerduty: Incident SRE-EU-003 acknowledged and resolved by rollback at +18m
tina_oncall: customer impact: small — some EU customers saw 502/500s between +3m and +10m, max 7 minutes. no data loss, no long-lived errors reported.
alice: I'll open an incident ticket with timeline and attach logs (will include PR that caused gpu_mode addition)
ben: quick root cause: config-generator introduced an optional field without updating runtime schema. fix: either make generator align with runtime, or add schema-forward compatibility in runtime
carlos: follow-up: add schema-check unit in release pipeline and a deploy-gate to catch this earlier
diana: agree. we'll schedule postmortem and add action items. Tina will hand off to next oncall for follow-up
tina_oncall: handing off to next oncall at shift end. leaving runbook notes in incident ticket. looping in infra-sre for postmortem
infra-bot: smoke checks stable for 20m, no regressions detected
diana: thanks everyone — incident closed for now, reopen if we see regression :thumbsup:
